Former India captain Rahul Dravid nominated to senior board for 2030 Commonwealth Games preparations

31 Oct 2026, 05:12 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: news.abplive.com

3 min read

Key takeawaysThe report notes that the board will also include other private‑sector and government representatives, but their names were not disclosed.

Overview

A report cited by ABP Live says the Union Sports Ministry has nominated former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid and badminton star Saina Nehwal to represent the sporting community on the board of the organising company for the 2030 Commonwealth Games, which India is set to host.

Confirmed nominations

  • Rahul Dravid – former India cricket captain, former head coach of the men’s national team (2021‑2024).
  • Saina Nehwal – former world‑number‑one badminton player.
  • The nominations were announced in a report by *The Indian Express* and reproduced by ABP Live.
  • Both athletes are listed as *representatives of the sports sector* on the proposed board.

The report notes that the board will also include other private‑sector and government representatives, but their names were not disclosed.

Dravid’s relevant experience

  • Board of Advisors, GoSports Foundation (since 2014) – supports Indian athletes across disciplines.
  • Rahul Dravid Athlete Mentorship Programme – provides guidance to emerging sportspersons.
  • Head coach of India’s men’s cricket team (late 2021‑2024) – oversaw the team’s T20 World Cup win in 2024 and multiple finals appearances.
  • These roles are cited as evidence of his familiarity with athlete‑centred administration, though the report does not claim any prior involvement with multi‑sport event planning.

Potential practical implications

  • Athlete perspective: Dravid and Nehwal could influence venue design, scheduling, and athlete services to reflect on‑ground needs.
  • Credibility: Their high public profiles may help attract sponsorship and public support for the Games.
  • Governance balance: Inclusion of sports figures alongside private‑sector and government members aims to create a more diversified decision‑making body.

Status of acceptance

  • Neither Dravid nor Nehwal has publicly confirmed whether they will accept the proposed positions.
  • The report describes the nominations as *proposed* and indicates that final appointments will depend on the athletes’ consent.

How to verify the announcement

  1. Check the original *Indian Express* article – the ABP Live piece references it; locating the original story will provide the primary source.
  2. Monitor official statements – the Union Sports Ministry, the Commonwealth Games organising company, or the athletes’ personal/official social‑media accounts may issue confirmations.
  3. Look for government press releases – the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports typically publishes formal appointment notices.
  4. Follow reputable news outlets – subsequent coverage by agencies such as Reuters, PTI, or major Indian newspapers will likely report any confirmed appointments.

Unknowns / open questions

  • Exact responsibilities: The report does not detail the specific duties Dravid and Nehwal would hold on the board.
  • Timeline: No dates are given for when the board will be formally constituted or when the Games planning milestones will begin.
  • Compensation or contractual terms: No information on remuneration, term length, or performance metrics.
  • Impact on existing cricket or badminton administration: It is unclear whether the athletes’ involvement will affect their current roles in sport‑specific bodies.

--- *The article is based on information reported by ABP Live, which cites *The Indian Express*. No direct quotes from Dravid, Nehwal, or government officials were available in the source.*
